_doc: Per-image spec overrides applied on top of tools/question_images/manifest.json by render.py (round 2026-11-06). Keys = imageName.

20._why: user: sign at a curb with parked cars and a street behind it, square to the camera. Camera on the sidewalk looking back across the street (the only way the street, not a building wall, is behind a 0.3 m sign at the 15 % rule distance); sign at eye level; two cars parked at the curb behind it

149._why: vehicle_rear template can't meet the 15 % rule without the car hiding the sign; car stopped at the stop line instead

54._why: island-mounted marker: camera in the inner lane right of the island (size limited by headroom: 0.3 x 0.9 m); raised concrete median island with a rounded curb nose; marker on the nose (Wa-33L stripes slope down to the right = pass on the right); median-mounted: the 55-65 % rule is mirrored (sign at 40 %) so the travel lanes, which are to the RIGHT of a median sign, stay in view

56._why: island-mounted sign: camera in the inner lane right of the island

119._why: highway: camera on the right shoulder 1.2 m left of the sign so the sign isn't seen edge-on

148._why: highway: camera on the right shoulder 1.2 m left of the sign so the sign isn't seen edge-on

44._why: user: road crossing the tracks, crossbuck + flasher mast on the right shoulder, camera at eye height looking along the road. The crossbuck sits ~4 m up, so at the 15 % distance the camera would look at the sky; at ~8 % it stays level

100._why: road clearly passes under the bridge (abutments just outside the shoulders). Clearance built to 3.9 m to match the official Wa-26 artwork (current image says 3.8 m; artwork can't be changed)

81._why: user: add the two yellow beacons (current image: arms out from the post at the base of the pentagon, beacons beside MAXIMUM 40) and lower the camera so the road shows; sign 9 % of width so the camera stands back and looks level

114._why: user: show the road with the crossover markings and lower the camera. Ra-4 stands at the crossover (ladder starts at the sign). Sign 7.5 % of width: the only way the 3.3 m-high sign and the markings both fit the 2.4:1 frame

99._why: user: add an on-ramp merging from the right. Rural shoulder road (a ramp doesn't fit a curbed residential street); ramp swings in from the right, acceleration lane, taper ends at 150 m | review3: sign moved to the left so the ramp is close and large: full-width 3.75 m lane on a smooth curve, level with the highway, 45 m taper, gore wedge, edge lines, shoulder

46._why: user: show the median beginning - island starts 80 m ahead with a rounded curbed nose, in view beyond the sign

48._why: user: add the two-way left-turn lane pavement arrows (opposing pairs of bent arrows in the centre lane, placed where the camera sees the road); sign centred over the centre (TWLTL) lane

91._why: review3: camera at the top of the grade looking DOWN an 18% descent; the road drops ~20 m over 110 m into a valley and continues flat to the horizon (no crest edge); terrain follows the road, trees snapped to it

111._why: user: full railway track across the road ahead (rails, ties, ballast, crossing surface), continuing into the fields past both frame edges | review3: track closer (30 m), raised ballast, ties on ballast, rails, crossing panel across the full road+shoulders; crossing mast dropped (its crossbuck was cut by the frame top)

154._why: user: roundabout visible ahead (central island, circular lane, yield lines, entry splitter island) that the road leads into. No '300 m' tab: no official artwork exists (see REVIEW2_CHANGES deviation 3)

103._why: user: realistic, much taller rock cliff/rock cut rising beside the shoulder; stepped face (no overhang), foot buried (no gap), fallen rocks on the shoulder

155._why: chevron: the sharp left bend must be visible. Large-format chevron (1.2 m) so the 15 % rule puts the camera ~11 m back, where the bend (starting 8 m ahead of the camera) is in frame left of the sign

92._why: review3: tracks closer (28 m) and skewed 30 deg (the sign is the angled-crossing warning) so rails, ties, raised ballast and crossing panels are readable across the full frame width

89._why: review3: bridge closer so both parapets read; sloped earth banks into a real water channel under the deck; matching parapet + handrail on both sides

117._why: review3: one signal head moved next to the sign so the whole head stays inside the frame with >=5% margin; only the red lamp is lit

104._why: review3: tall sign - camera raised so the lot ground (stalls) shows behind it
